title: Protection visas are for asylum seekers

sections.heading: Eligibility for a Protection visa
sections.text:
Protection visas are for people (or their family members) who meet the definition of a refugee or meet complementary protection criteria. A person is a refugee if they would face persecution in their home country for any of the following reasons:

- race
- religion
- nationality
- membership of a particular social group
- political opinion.

A person is owed complementary protection if there are grounds to believe they would face a real risk of significant harm if returned to their home country.

To apply for a Protection visa, you must be in Australia, having arrived on a valid visa and been immigration cleared on arrival.

When you apply for a Protection visa you are seeking asylum in Australia from your home country. If you can legally enter and safely live in another country, we will not grant you a Protection visa in Australia. This means a country other than your home country.

Read more about Australia's protection obligations.

sections.heading: Travel restrictions attached to your Protection visa
sections.text:
If you apply for a Protection visa, you will be granted either a Bridging visa A, C, or E. The type depends on your substantive visa and lawful status at the time. None of these visas allow you to return to Australia if you leave. You cannot apply for a Bridging visa B to allow you to travel.

If you leave Australia for any reason while we process your Protection visa application, you may not be able to return. This also applies if you leave while waiting for a review outcome.

If we grant you a Protection visa, you cannot travel to the country you have obtained protection from without permission from the Australian Government. This applies even if your family lives there.

Learn more about Bridging visas.

sections.heading: If we refuse your Protection visa
sections.text:
We refuse approximately 85% of Protection visa applications as they do not meet the requirements for the visa. Applications from some nationalities have refusal rates close to 100%. If we refuse your Protection visa application:

- you cannot apply for most other visas while you are in Australia
- you will need to leave Australia if you do not hold a valid visa
- you and your family may find it harder to visit Australia in the future
- your refusal will stay on your immigration record for life
- it can impact future visa applications to other countries outside of Australia.

If we refuse your Protection visa application and you choose to have your decision reviewed at the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), you will be required to pay a review fee. If you do not pay the fee the ART will not be able to conduct a review of your decision. The fee is indexed each year and is currently $1863.50.

If the ART agrees with our decision to refuse you a Protection visa, you will not get this money back.

The Australian Government will detain and remove refused Protection visa applicants who no longer have a right to stay in Australia. These enforcement activities help maintain the integrity of Australia’s immigration system.

If we detain and remove you from Australia after we refuse your Protection visa application, you may need to pay back the cost of your removal. This could be thousands of dollars.

You can read more about what can happen if an application for a Protection visa is refused by viewing Protection visa applicant stories.

sections.heading: Your responsibilities when submitting a Protection visa application
sections.text:
When you submit a Protection visa application, it is your responsibility to ensure that all the information you provide is correct. This applies even if somebody else completes and submits your application for you. Make sure that you understand what you are applying for and what information you are providing in the application before anyone helps you to complete or submit it.

If you apply for a Protection visa when you do not need Australia’s protection, you delay processing for people who are genuinely seeking asylum.

There are serious consequences if you lie or provide bogus documents in a visa application. You could face large fines, possible jail for up to 10 years, or both.

If you are found to have lied or provided bogus documents after your visa has been granted, your Protection visa can be cancelled. A refused Protection visa application or cancelled Protection visa can impact future Australian visas for you and your family. It can also affect future visa applications to other countries outside of Australia.

Communities in Australia play an important role in stopping the spread of false information to people considering applying for a Protection visa. This includes spreading awareness of the risks of submitting false or misleading information and using an unregistered migration adviser.

If someone asks you to write a support letter for their Protection visa application, encourage them to seek legal advice. They can get free advice from a specialist refugee and immigration legal provider in their state or territory (see below).

sections.heading: Seek professional advice before you apply
sections.text:
Before you apply for a Protection visa, you should get professional advice from a registered migration agent or an Australian legal practitioner. These are the only people in Australia allowed to charge for migration advice.

If you do not use a registered migration agent or an Australian legal practitioner, you risk getting incorrect advice that could harm your chances of staying in Australia.

To check if someone is a registered migration agent, search the online register on the Office of Migration Agents Registration Authority (OMARA) website.

You can also:

- view the steps to choose a registered migration agent
- find out more about getting help from an Australian legal practitioner
- learn more about who can help you with your application in Australia.

You can get free and confidential advice from a specialist, government-funded refugee and immigration legal provider in your state or territory. These providers can help you:

- find out if you are eligible for a Protection visa or another more suitable visa
- understand the application process
- understand the implications of a Protection visa refusal
- complete and lodge a Protection visa application if required.

sections.heading: Beware of visa scammers
sections.text:
Beware of visa scams and scam agents pretending to be official migration professionals. Scam agents often advertise their services on social media and in chat groups. They sometimes tell applicants to submit false documents, or to give false or misleading information when applying for a Protection visa.

Some scammers may even apply for a Protection visa for you without your knowledge, telling you they have applied for a visa that will let you stay in Australia to work.

If someone promises you a Protection visa, or demands a large upfront payment to ‘fast-track’ your application, it is probably a scam. Find out what to look out for in visa scams.

If someone tries to illegally give you immigration assistance, you can tell us by using the Border Watch Online Report. You do not have to give your name.

sections.heading: Other visa options
sections.text:
Other visas may be more suited to your circumstances if you do not meet the eligibility for a Protection visa.

To find the right visa for you, Explore your options.

sections.heading: You can withdraw your Protection visa application at any time
sections.text:
You may decide you no longer want to proceed with your application. This may be because you are not an asylum seeker and do not meet the criteria for a Protection visa, or there is another visa that better suits your circumstances, or you wish to return to your home country.

You can withdraw your application at any time before a decision on your application is made. There is no penalty for withdrawing an application for a Protection visa.

To withdraw your application:

- Log in to ImmiAccount
- Select ‘View’ to open your application
- Select ‘Update details’
- Select ‘Withdrawal of a visa application’

Learn more about how to withdraw a visa application.

sections.heading: Getting help before or after your temporary visa expires
sections.text:
To find out if your visa is expiring soon or has already expired, fill in your details at Visa Entitlement Verification Online (VEVO).

Our Immigration Status Resolution Service can help if you do not have a valid visa and have become an unlawful non-citizen. They can also give accurate information on how to avoid becoming unlawful in the future.

Status resolution officers can:

- explain your visa options
- tell you how decisions you make can affect your options later
- help you plan to leave Australia
- refer you to other services where necessary.

Find out more at Status Resolution Service.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
A Protection (subclass 866) visa allows a person to live in Australia permanently. It is for people at real risk of significant harm or persecution in their home country. This visa is not for people who just want to stay longer in Australia to work.

Protection visa applications are processed quickly and have a decision made much faster than in previous years. This means a quicker grant of Protection visas to those in need, and a swift refusal for those who are not eligible.

Do not apply for a Protection visa if you do not need asylum in Australia. We quickly refuse applicants who do not meet Protection visa criteria.

If you are considering applying for a Protection visa, we strongly encourage you to seek professional advice before you apply. Seek this advice from a registered migration agent or an Australian legal practitioner.
